themes.name: Instrument Development and Psychometric Validation in Engineering Education
themes.definition: This theme encompasses research focused on the design, adaptation, and rigorous psychometric testing of measurement instruments such as scales, questionnaires, and rubrics. Studies typically employ exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, reliability coefficients (e.g., Cronbach's alpha), item analysis, and validity evidence to ensure the tools are reliable and valid for assessing various constructs in engineering education.
evidence: [RGASR6Q5] This study addresses this gap by developing and validating a new instrument, the Engineering Students’ Attitudes Toward Practical Work (ESAPW) questionnaire
[GMEMS46N] This study validates the Compassionate Engagement and Action Scales for Self and Others (CEAS) for use with undergraduate engineering students in the United States.

[KU4TN5MB] This research paper describes the development and initial validation of a questionnaire to assess students' attitudes toward engineering and their appreciation of the sociotechnical nature of engineering.

themes.name: Assessment of Generic, Transversal, and Professional Competencies
themes.definition: Research that develops or validates instruments to measure broad professional skills often called generic or transversal competencies, such as teamwork, communication, lifelong learning, entrepreneurial abilities, and innovation. These competencies are seen as essential for workplace readiness and are frequently assessed through self-report or performance tasks.
evidence: [WE7WVA4B] Pre-professional internships are crucial in training civil engineering students, as they foster the development of generic competencies essential for professional success and workplace adaptability.

[SL7257LZ] This study reports on a reliable and valid instrument that measures engineering students' perceptions of their competency levels. ... Students perceived they are most competent in teamwork and lifelong learning competencies and less competent in entrepreneurial competencies.
[2IGUA9SF] This tool provides a robust basis for continuous improvement in teaching innovation, aligning academic training with labour market demands and global challenges for engineering graduates.

themes.name: Self-Efficacy and Engineering Identity Measurement
themes.definition: Studies aimed at creating and validating scales that capture engineering students' beliefs about their capabilities (self-efficacy) in specific skill areas (entrepreneurship, design, general engineering) and their identification with the engineering profession. These constructs are often linked to academic persistence, career intentions, and performance.
evidence: [LPJSUJ9V] This study’s aim is to evaluate the Romanian version of the Internet Entrepreneurial Self-Efficacy Scale (IESES), a new assessment scale for online entrepreneurial self-efficacy
[AIPHQE23] This study used the design activities and design competencies required by the industrial design process as items to develop an 'Industrial Design Self-Efficacy and Anxiety Scale'

[W2PMJWMT] Contribution: This paper shows that identification with engineering for engineering graduate students is positively and significantly predicted by engineering interest, competence, recognition, and interpersonal skills competence.

themes.name: Attitudes Toward Engineering and Practical Learning Experiences
themes.definition: Research that quantitatively assesses engineering students' attitudes toward practical work, the sociotechnical nature of the discipline, and the learning of professional skills. Instruments typically employ Likert-type items and are validated through factor analysis to reveal underlying dimensions of student perceptions.
evidence: [RGASR6Q5] The purpose of this study was to develop and validate a multidimensional instrument to measure the attitudes of engineering students toward practical work in Nigeria
[KU4TN5MB] development and initial validation of a questionnaire to assess students' attitudes toward engineering and their appreciation of the sociotechnical nature of engineering.
[PD6ENBV2] Using the Theory of Planned Behavior as an overarching framework, one explanation for skill development gaps may be students’ attitude towards learning professional skills.

themes.name: Rubric-Based Competency Assessment
themes.definition: A body of work that centers on the design, validation, and use of scoring rubrics to evaluate student competencies in engineering contexts, including laboratories, oral presentations, and online discussions. Emphasis is on content validity by expert judgment and inter-rater reliability as key quality indicators.
evidence: [ECTTSUXE] In the field of physics education, the application of Ribes' functional taxonomy for rubric design remains uncommon. ... This study aims to validate a rubric based on Ribes' five functional levels
[9HGRHX6A] In this paper, the importance of a properly designed rubric in the competency-based assessment process is emphasized.
[A3WRUNHT] This study aims to propose a competency assessment model for students in online discussion forums, using the Rubrics scoring tool and the Bloom's Taxonomy to define evaluation feedback.

themes.name: Research Competences and Investigative Skills
themes.definition: Studies that identify and measure the research skills required by engineering students, often for completing final projects. Instruments assess multiple dimensions such as intellectual elaboration, technical, and communicative competences, and frequently report high reliability indices for self-perception scales.
evidence: [84K6T4E3] The objective of this article is to identify the training needs perceived by university students in terms of research skills needed for drafting research projects.
[Y4ZKXXH4] the study focuses on analyzing the self-perception of the acquisition of research competences of mechanical and electrical engineering students

[84K6T4E3] The bibliographic review allowed us to identify three subcategories of investigative competences: a) Intellectual Elaboration Competences, b) Technical Competences and c) Communicative Competences.

themes.name: Critical, Reflective, and Representational Thinking Assessment
themes.definition: Instruments developed to measure higher-order cognitive skills in engineering, including critical thinking in automation control, reflective thinking during design problem solving, and representational competence with vectors. Validation methods include item analysis, reliability testing, and correlations with open-ended problem-solving performance.
evidence: [EPIKGTEL] This study developes and validates an Automation Studio-based critical thinking assessment instrument for electrical engineering students, focusing on the ladder diagram concepts in automation control systems.

[RUGB95IU] In this study, we have developed and validated a novel self-reporting questionnaire as an efficient instrument to explore reflection, called Assessing Reflective Thinking in Solving Design Problems ( ARTiD ).
[AKZVTZER] This paper presents development work for a new assessment instrument designed to measure representational competence with vectors in an engineering mechanics context.

themes.name: Affective and Ethical Competence Assessment
themes.definition: Research targeting the assessment of values, compassion, and socio-emotional competencies in engineering students. These studies adapt instruments from psychology (e.g., Compassionate Engagement and Action Scales) or create value statements using Thurstone scaling, focusing on affective learning outcomes and professional ethics.
evidence: [GMEMS46N] Compassion, defined as sensitivity to suffering in oneself and others coupled with a commitment to alleviate and prevent it, is increasingly recognized as a vital socio-emotional competency in professional education.

[DNK3JI3N] This exploratory study aimed at examining assessment of dispositional knowledge in the context of global software engineering (GSE). It focused on the development and use of a set of instruments for assessing affective domain student learning of global IT/software engineering (SE) professional values.

data.meta_observations: The batch is overwhelmingly dominated by quantitative instrument development and validation studies employing factor analysis and Cronbach's alpha. There is a strong emphasis on self-report questionnaires and rubrics for competencies and attitudes. Quality notes indicate many abstracts are missing objectives, conclusions, or quantitative data; accordingly, only explicitly stated content was used. The closed set of keys was strictly adhered to, and fabricated quotes were avoided.
data.grounding_notes: All evidence is verbatim from provided abstracts. Article JKK5M2EG has a truncated abstract and was only included based on its title, which explicitly indicates attitude measurement; it was excluded from the psychometric validation theme due to missing methodological details. The meta-theme 'Instrument Development and Psychometric Validation' overlaps with all substantive themes; its article list includes almost every abstract except the aforementioned one. Frequencies are based on counts within this batch.
